chunks.rationale: Pure mapping contract for issue #549, independent of spawn. Start here: bare `cancelled`/`canceled` is a stop; leftover result text must not override that; remaining error_during_execution cases keep CLI errors[]/stderr and never mention `result subtype`; session-lost still adds the reset follow-up without duplicating the CLI line; empty input falls back to `Run error`.
risks: Stop is an exact-token match. A CLI that says `cancelled: permission denied` in one string stays a failure (intentional) but a CLI that only says `cancelled` for an unrecoverable tool death will look like a user stop.

The suite never feeds subtype into the assertion besides checking it is absent from copy — a regression that puts subtype back in failText is caught; a regression that ignores errors[] and shows a generic Run error is also caught.

chunks.rationale: classifyClaudeResultError plus the claude-stream `type === result` terminal. The old `Run error: result subtype ${ev.subtype}` path is gone. Bare cancel mirrors stopRun (idle, `Run stopped`, notify stopped, lastError cleared). Other failures go through markRunFailed with CLI text. Error result payloads are no longer copied into an assistant bubble.
risks: stderr is read at result time via handle.getStderr(). stdout and stderr are different streams, so a result line can land before the stderr chunk. Empty errors[] then becomes a generic `Run error` until/unless stderr has already arrived. The integration test delays 40ms after writing stderr to hide that race.
CLI-side cancel does not cascade crew the way stopRun does. A worker that self-cancels leaves siblings running. That matches 'this thread's run ended', not 'the user stopped the orchestrator'.
notifyRunTerminal('stopped') skips afterFailedTurn, so an orchestrator will not get a failure wake from a gated-tool auto-cancel. Same as a user Stop.
Success no longer nulls sessionId on a hypothetical success+session-lost combo. That combination never existed in the wild.

chunks.rationale: getStderr() on the handle so the result path can attach a stderr tail without waiting for process exit (which no-ops once sawResult is set).
risks: The spawn-failure stub returns getStderr: () => "". Callers that assume a live buffer must tolerate an empty string.
Tail is still 64KiB; a noisy CLI can push the useful last line out of the unique-line merge if errors[] already filled shown.

chunks.rationale: Fake scenarios (result-cancelled, result-exec-error, result-exec-error-stderr, result-cancelled-plus-error) plus session-lost assertions updated to forbid `result subtype` / `error_during_execution` in user-facing copy. Read after the mapper so you see the terminal shape (idle vs failed, work-log label, lastError).
risks: result-exec-error-stderr is timing-sensitive: if the 40ms delay is not enough on a loaded CI runner, the test fails even though the mapper is correct.

orch-server.test.js still fixtures the old `Run error: result subtype error_during_execution` string. That is mock thread_status data, not runner output — do not 'fix' it as if the runner still produced it.

A Grok permission auto-cancel that still emits this event will now look like a user Stop (idle, no Retry turn). That is the requested shape, but it can hide the underlying missing prompt channel (#3 / #177) if the user only notices a quiet stop.
jsdom/Electron UI is not exercised; Retry-turn absence follows from status idle + event text `Run stopped` (retryTurn.ts only lights on failed or `Run interrupted`).
